exposure: mother's perception of inadequate pain management
cohort: 300 pregnant women who attended the labor ward of the Specialty Hospital in Amman, Jordan between September 1, 2019, and June 1, 2020, with a mean age of 29.5 years and mean gestational age of 38.6 weeks
finding: Antenatal, peripartum, and neonatal variables, such as obstetric complications, mode of delivery, pain management, prematurity, low Apgar scores, low birth weight, NICU admission, and less frequent rooming-in, were associated with lower rates of early initiation of breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Caesarean section (both overall, performed on maternal request, and under general anesthesia) and assisted vaginal delivery were associated with lower rates of early initiation of breastfeeding.
